utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would we please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, good afternoon everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-83-T, The Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes. Good afternoon, Mr. President. Kyle Wood, Aditya Menon, legal intern Sarah Houlihan, for the Prosecution, assisted by Alma Imamovic our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, good afternoon to my learned colleagues from the Office of the Prosecutor, and to everyone in and around the courtroom. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson for the Defence of General Rasim Delic, with our legal assistant Lana Deljkic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Madam Vidovic or Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was to deal with the witness this afternoon; and, therefore, I'm standing to address the Bench. I must inform you that the Defence team has taken the decision not to call the witness this afternoon. Today, we are had an opportunity to carry out a consultation with the witness; and, as a result, we decided that we wouldn't call him. I apologise to my learned friends on the opposite bench for any inconvenience that they may have been caused and, indeed, to the Trial Chamber as well. Also, I would like to put on record our gratitude to the American government for the assistance that they have provided to us, and it was very gratefully received. There we have it, Your Honours, in a nutshell. The decision was taken; and, therefore, there will be no witness this afternoon. I can also confirm to that you the witness was due to be our final witness in this case, and we will not be calling any further witness as part of the Rasim Delic case. So, effectively, Your Honours, we have concluded the Defence case. What I can notify you of is that we filed our second bar table motion this morning. I was informed that it was filed before lunch. I haven't myself had a chance to confirm whether or not that this is the case. My understanding is that that motion was filed this morning, but essentially that is the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Formally, the Defence rests?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just one little housekeeping matter. The Trial Chamber renders its oral decision concerning the admission of exhibits. The Trial Chamber's admission of Exhibits 1316 and 1317 on the 17th of March, 2008 has been subject to an interlocutory appeal and a ruling by the Appeals Chamber of the 15th April 2008. The Trial Chamber has made its subsequent admission of Exhibits 1375 and 1376 contingent on the outcome of that appeal. The Trial Chamber holds that Exhibits 1316, 1317 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Shall I start over again? Okay. The Trial Chamber renders an oral decision concerning the admission of exhibits. The Trial Chamber's admission of Exhibits 1316 and 1317 on the 17th of March, 2008 has been subject to an interlocutory appeal and a ruling by the Appeals Chambers of the 15th April 2008. The Trial Chamber has made its subsequent admission of Exhibits 1375 and 1376 contingent on the outcome of that appeal. The Trial Chamber holds that Exhibits 1316, 1317, 1375, and 1376 shall be expunged from the trial record. A written decision giving reasons will follow in due course. Is the transcript on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the Chamber have to adjourn to a specific date or to a date to be arranged? Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: The Prosecution has nothing further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence also has nothing further to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Wood, does this mean that the Prosecution does not intend to call in for rebuttal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. In that event, then the matter stands adjourned to a date to be arranged. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: sine die

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.24 p.m.,
